criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First two lines name Governor Dunleavy, a specific June 18 deadline, and the structural tension (state authority vs. federal preemption) in under 210 chars. No dollar amount in the hook itself prevents a 10.

criteria.name: Industry relevance
criteria.notes: Every story is Alaska-anchored with a named sector consequence: compliance/law (HB 239), aviation labor (AI Crew Solutions UAT), service-sector automation ROI (minimum wage), tribal energy (DOE C-MAP), dual-use autonomy (XPRIZE). XPRIZE bullet thin on AK business consequence; C-MAP drops the per-project range.

criteria.name: Factual density
criteria.notes: Named specifics in nearly every sentence: vote tallies, dates, named individuals (Scheideman, Amodei), vendor (AI Crew Solutions), legislation (HB 239, Ballot Measure 1), dollar figures. Slight dip in the mid-post preemption framing paragraph.

criteria.name: Source quality
criteria.notes: HB 239 double-sourced with legislative primary; AI Crew Solutions union primary; preemption sourced to named ADN op-ed + Roll Call background; minimum wage single secondary (KTUU); XPRIZE background-context with a 'reportedly' hedge. No unsourced stats stated as fact.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Replicates post_001.md analytical register exactly: 'conventional framing... false-clean option' structural diagnosis, crisp declarative punches, tight bullet block, no influencer cadence or hype.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: 450 body words, 2794 total chars under the 3000 cap, tight 2-4 sentence paragraphs, one 3-item single-clause bullet block. The single-sentence transition adds a minor scan interruption.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Binary, specific to the central tension, debatable across stakeholders, no softener or CTA.

criteria.name: Business actionability
criteria.notes: Surfaces the June 18 HB 239 deadline, the July 2 C-MAP window, and the AI Crew Solutions UAT as concrete revisit triggers.

one_sentence_fix: Attribute the $14 minimum-wage figure to Alaska DOL / Ballot Measure 1 directly rather than a single TV outlet, and flag the XPRIZE bullet as out-of-window background context.
